resources.string: Cinema turns on whenever your phone is in landscape: sound stays anchored to the screen, dialogue is locked to its centre, effects spread wider and further back, and the added delay is lower for lip-sync.
Cinema is always on: sound anchored to the screen, dialogue locked to its centre, wide effects, lower delay.
Music settings are used in landscape too.

Every instrument gets its own fixed place in the room, re-rendered in real time. Android asks once to share audio; Pause keeps it, so you won\'t be asked again until you turn Spatial5 off or restart the phone.
No permission prompt and no added delay: head tracking is applied directly to every app. Lighter than Immersive 3D, best for video.
Tip: keep Dolby Atmos on in Standard. Dolby puts the sound around you, Spatial5 moves it with your head.
Tip: turn Dolby Atmos off while Immersive 3D is on, so the sound isn\'t virtualised twice.
Finds the best stage and room for each song
The front camera follows your head; the gyroscope fills in between frames. Nothing is recorded.
Uses only the phone\'s motion. Keep the phone in a pocket so it turns with you.
Sound stays put even when the phone moves
Cinema is on: sound follows the screen
Scene slowly follows you to a new direction
Pause Camera When Screen Is Off

When Android asks to share your screen, choose \"Entire screen\": only audio is used, and nothing is recorded or leaves your phone.\n\nHRTF data: MIT Media Lab KEMAR (Gardner & Martin). Head model: \"Lee Perry-Smith\" scan by Infinite Realities, CC BY 3.0.
